content.text:
You can now drag the Tweaks button to one of three spots, and it snaps to the nearest one when you let go. Type check, lint, format check and build pass. I tried it in the browser at desktop (1440) and phone (390) widths. Nothing is committed.

- **Bottom-right** (the default): where it was before.
- **Top-right**: under the top bar. The panel opens downward from there.
- **Sidebar**: the bottom of the left sidebar. The sidebar makes room for it, so it sits below the persona and transport footer instead of covering it. On phones there is no sidebar on screen, so it goes to the bottom-left corner.

While you drag, dashed outlines show the three spots, and the one it will snap to is highlighted. A press that moves less than 5px still just opens the panel, and dropping the button never opens it.

The position is saved with your other tweaks, so it stays after a reload. The panel also has a **Button position** picker at the bottom, so you can move it with the keyboard too.

If the window is too short for the open panel, the panel now scrolls instead of running off the screen.

I restarted your dev server (`mise run stop`, then `mise run dev`, which also restarts the speech-to-text proxy on 3001). It was still serving the old `globals.css` even after the file changed, which the project notes already record as a known issue. If you had it running in a terminal, that terminal's process is gone; the new one is running in the background.

The changes:
- [lib/tweaks-dock.ts](lib/tweaks-dock.ts): the three spots and the "nearest spot" rule.
- [hooks/use-dock-drag.ts](hooks/use-dock-drag.ts): the drag itself, and telling a drag apart from a click.
- [app/styles/tweaks-dock.css](app/styles/tweaks-dock.css): where each spot is on screen.
- [tweaks-panel.tsx](components/tsubaki/tweaks-panel.tsx), [use-tweaks.ts](hooks/use-tweaks.ts) and [app-shell.tsx](components/tsubaki/app-shell.tsx): wiring, the saved setting, and the sidebar making room.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The spots are defined only in CSS. The dashed outlines are real elements that use the same CSS classes as the button, and the drag measures them to find the nearest spot. So changing the top-bar height or the gap in the stylesheet can't put the button and the snapping out of step.
- The button follows the pointer by changing its offset from its current spot. It never switches to free left/top coordinates, so letting go only means changing which spot it belongs to and dropping the offset.
- Snapping picks the closest spot in a straight line (`nearestDock`). If you would rather it go by which part of the screen you drop it in, so that dropping anywhere over the sidebar always means "sidebar", that's the one function to change.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Shell layer — Settings grid order and the mobile shell (sections drawer,
   full-parity pages). Loaded after styles.css and i18n.css.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* ── Settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Full-width band above the 2×2 grid, so the grid keeps the app's order:
   AUDIO IN | AUDIO OUT, BEHAVIOUR | TOOLS. */
.pp-settings-sec-wide { grid-column: 1 / -1; border-right: 0; }

/* ── Mobile: menu button + sections drawer ────────────────────────────── */

.pp-menu-btn {
  appearance: none; cursor: pointer;
  display: inline-grid; place-items: center;
  width: 28px; height: 28px; margin-left: -6px;
  background: transparent; color: var(--ink);
  border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0;
  flex: 0 0 auto;
}
.pp-menu-btn:hover { border-color: var(--line); }
.pp-menu-btn[aria-expanded="true"] { background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); }
.pp-mobile .pp-topbar { gap: 12px; }

/* The layer spans the artboard (.pp-mobile is position: relative). Closed, it
   is visibility-hidden so the drawer's buttons leave the tab order. */
.pp-drawer-layer {
  position: absolute; inset: 0;
  z-index: 40;
  visibility: hidden;
  transition: visibility 0s linear 0.22s;
}
.pp-drawer-layer.open { visibility: visible; transition-delay: 0s; }
.pp-drawer-scrim {
  position: absolute; inset: 0;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 38%, transparent);
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity 0.22s ease;
}
.pp-drawer-layer.open .pp-drawer-scrim { opacity: 1; }
.pp-drawer {
  position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0;
  width: 240px; max-width: 80%;
  display: flex;
  border-right: 1px solid var(--line);
  box-shadow: 4px 0 0 var(--line);
  transform: translateX(calc(-100% - 6px));
  transition: transform 0.22s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1);
}
.pp-drawer-layer.open .pp-drawer { transform: none; }
/* The reused desktop Sidebar fills the drawer; it already owns its border. */
.pp-drawer .pp-side { flex: 1 1 auto; border-right: 0; padding-top: 22px; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .pp-drawer, .pp-drawer-scrim { transition: none; }
}

/* ── Mobile: full-parity pages ────────────────────────────────────────── */

.pp-mobile-page { flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; }

.pp-mobile .pp-page-hd { flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: flex-start; gap: 12px; }
.pp-mobile .pp-page-hd-r { flex-wrap: wrap; }
.pp-mobile .pp-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
/* Provider notes don't fit at 390px; the active provider's specs below the

   under the call controls now that no tab bar sits between them. */

/* PREVIEW tag — a mock surface (tools). Dashed accent outline reads as
   "not live" without shouting; sits inline after a section/popover label. */

  display: inline-block;
  margin-left: 8px;
  padding: 1px 5px;
  font-size: 8.5px; letter-spacing: 0.14em; line-height: 1.4;

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Language layer — EN / 日本語. Loaded after styles.css.
   The app root carries lang + data-lang, so every rule cascades from .pp-app
   instead of per-element .pp-ja opt-ins.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Per-glyph fallback, always on: Latin stays IBM Plex Mono / Newsreader; kana
   and kanji fall through to Noto. Plex Mono and Newsreader carry no CJK, so
   without this the OS picks (and the 日本語 label in EN mode renders in
   whatever it finds). */
/* --pp-ja-sans / --pp-ja-serif are set per artboard from the Tweaks panel
   (jaFontVars in i18n.jsx); Noto is the default. */
.pp-app {
  --pp-ja-sans: "Noto Sans JP";
  --pp-ja-serif: "Noto Serif JP";
  font-family: "IBM Plex Mono", var(--pp-ja-sans), ui-monospace, monospace;
}
.pp-app :is(.pp-h1, .pp-caption, .pp-mobile-caption, .pp-turn-text, .pp-persona-desc, .pp-ja-greet-t) {
  font-family: "Newsreader", var(--pp-ja-serif), ui-serif, Georgia, serif;
}

/* ── Japanese typography ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Kinsoku (no 。、」 at line start) and breaking inside long kana runs. */
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] { line-break: strict; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }

/* Italic Japanese is a synthesized slant — set the serif contexts upright,
   with the extra leading CJK text needs. */
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] :is(.pp-h1, .pp-caption, .pp-mobile-caption, .pp-turn-text, .pp-persona-desc) {
  font-style: normal;
  font-synthesis: none;
}
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] .pp-h1 { font-size: 38px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.02em; line-height: 1.15; }
.pp-app.pp-mobile[data-lang="ja"] .pp-h1 { font-size: 24px; }
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] .pp-caption { font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.8; }
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] .pp-mobile-caption { font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; }
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] .pp-turn-text { font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.8; }
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] .pp-persona-desc { font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.85; }
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] .pp-lede { line-height: 1.8; }

/* ALL-CAPS tracked labels don't translate: text-transform is a no-op on kana,
   wide tracking fragments words, and 8–9px kanji is illegible. Tighten the
   tracking everywhere and lift the smallest labels to a 10.5px floor. */
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] :is(
  .pp-side-eyebrow, .pp-spec-l, .pp-field-hd, .pp-turn-hd, .pp-table thead th,
  .pp-mobile-tab, .pp-mobile-sheet-handle, .pp-tools-pop-hd, .pp-tools-pop-foot,
  .pp-switch, .pp-lang-field-l, .pp-mobile-status, .pp-ja-greet-l,
  .pp-ja-support, .pp-prov-inset-l, .pp-tool-status, .pp-call-manual-hint,
  .pp-ja-mark, .pp-trait
) {
  font-size: 10.5px;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
}
.pp-app[data-lang="ja"] :is(
  .pp-h-eyebrow, .pp-nav-item, .pp-tag, .pp-hr-label, .pp-label, .pp-btn,
  .pp-call-state, .pp-call-state-sub, .pp-transcript-hd, .pp-topbar-status,
  .pp-failover, .pp-persona-drop, .pp-mobile-state, .pp-micsel-mute,
  .pp-persona-accent, .pp-brand-sub, .pp-side-foot
) {
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
}

/* ── Session routing strip ────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Zero-height sticky slot: the strip overlays the top of whatever page is
   open (no layout shift) and stays in view while that page scrolls. */
.pp-route-slot {
  position: sticky; top: 0;
  height: 0; overflow: visible;
  z-index: 20;
  flex: 0 0 auto;
}
.pp-route-slot .pp-failover {
  position: absolute; top: 12px; left: 28px; right: 28px;
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 var(--line);
}
.pp-mobile .pp-route-slot .pp-failover { top: 8px; left: 14px; right: 14px; margin: 0; }
/* A forced language drop is a warning, not a confirmation — keep it dashed. */
.pp-failover.pp-route-downgrade.done,
.pp-failover.pp-route-unavailable { border-style: dashed; }

/* orb.css — the voice visualizer (3 styles × call states) and the soundbars,
   moved out of orb.jsx's injected <style>. Plus the artboard scrollbar reset
   that the original index.html carried inline. */

.pp-app *::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 0; height: 0; }
.pp-app * { scrollbar-width: none; }

@keyframes pp-orb-breath {
  0%, 100% { transform: scale(0.96); }
  50% { transform: scale(1.04); }
}
@keyframes pp-orb-listen {
  0%, 100% { transform: scale(0.99); }
  50% { transform: scale(1.02); }
}
@keyframes pp-orb-speak {
  0% { transform: scale(0.94) rotate(0deg); }
  25% { transform: scale(1.07) rotate(2deg); }
  50% { transform: scale(0.97) rotate(-1deg); }
  75% { transform: scale(1.05) rotate(1deg); }
  100% { transform: scale(0.94) rotate(0deg); }
}
@keyframes pp-orb-spin { from { transform: rotate(0); } to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }
@keyframes pp-orb-spin-r { from { transform: rotate(360deg); } to { transform: rotate(0); } }
@keyframes pp-orb-noise { 0% { transform: translate(0,0); } 100% { transform: translate(-12px,-7px); } }
@keyframes pp-orb-ring {
  0% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 0.6; }
  100% { transform: scale(1.6); opacity: 0; }
}
@keyframes pp-bar {
  0%, 100% { transform: scaleY(0.25); }
  50% { transform: scaleY(1); }
}

.pp-orb {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
  width: var(--pp-orb-size, 320px);
  height: var(--pp-orb-size, 320px);
  --pp-accent: #B0122F;
}
.pp-orb-core { width: 100%; height: 100%; position: relative; }
.pp-orb[data-state="idle"] .pp-orb-core { animation: pp-orb-breath 6s ease-in-out infinite; }
.pp-orb[data-state="listening"] .pp-orb-core { animation: pp-orb-listen 1.4s ease-in-out infinite; }
.pp-orb[data-state="speaking"] .pp-orb-core { animation: pp-orb-speak 2.2s ease-in-out infinite; }
.pp-orb[data-state="connecting"] .pp-orb-core { animation: pp-orb-breath 1.4s ease-in-out infinite; }
.pp-orb[data-state="ended"] .pp-orb-core { filter: grayscale(1) opacity(0.45); }

/* Ring pulse */
.pp-orb-ring {
  position: absolute; inset: 0;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
  border-radius: 50%;
  pointer-events: none;
  opacity: 0;
}
.pp-orb[data-state="listening"] .pp-orb-ring,
.pp-orb[data-state="speaking"]  .pp-orb-ring {
  animation: pp-orb-ring 2.4s ease-out infinite;
}
.pp-orb[data-state="speaking"] .pp-orb-ring-2 { animation-delay: 0.8s; }
.pp-orb[data-state="speaking"] .pp-orb-ring-3 { animation-delay: 1.6s; }

/* Gradient orb (default) — accent-driven two-tone. */
.pp-orb-grad {
  width: 100%; height: 100%; border-radius: 50%;
  background:
    radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%, rgba(255,255,255,0.85), transparent 40%),
    conic-gradient(from 0deg,
      var(--pp-accent),
      color-mix(in srgb, var(--pp-accent) 55%, #000),
      var(--pp-accent),
      color-mix(in srgb, var(--pp-accent) 70%, #1a0006),
      var(--pp-accent));
  filter: blur(0.5px);
  position: relative; overflow: hidden;
}
.pp-orb-grad::before {
  content: ""; position: absolute; inset: -8%;
  background:
    radial-gradient(circle at 70% 60%, rgba(255,255,255,0.5), transparent 40%),
    radial-gradient(circle at 20% 80%, rgba(0,0,0,0.25), transparent 50%);
  animation: pp-orb-spin 14s linear infinite;
  mix-blend-mode: overlay;
}
.pp-orb-grad::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 6%;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, rgba(255,255,255,0.55), transparent 55%);
  animation: pp-orb-spin-r 18s linear infinite;
}

/* Mono orb */
.pp-orb-mono {
  width: 100%; height: 100%; border-radius: 50%;
  background:
    radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%, #ffffff, #c4c0b6 30%, #2a2926 75%, #060604 100%);
  position: relative; overflow: hidden;
}
.pp-orb-mono::before {
  content:""; position:absolute; inset:0; border-radius:50%;
  background-image:
    repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, transparent 0 6px, rgba(0,0,0,0.15) 6px 7px);
  mix-blend-mode: multiply;
}
.pp-orb-mono::after {
  content:""; position:absolute; inset:8%;
  border-radius:50%;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5);
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 40% 30%, rgba(255,255,255,0.7), transparent 45%);
}
.pp-orb.dark .pp-orb-mono {
  background:
    radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%, #f4f2ed, #5a574e 30%, #161513 75%, #000 100%);
}

/* Particle orb — a gradient disc plus 280 seeded dots, laid out in % of the orb. */
.pp-orb-particle {
  width: 100%; height: 100%; border-radius: 50%;
  position: relative; overflow: hidden;
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, rgba(0,0,0,0.04), transparent 70%);
}
.pp-orb.dark .pp-orb-particle {
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, rgba(255,255,255,0.06), transparent 70%);
}
.pp-orb-pgrad { position: absolute; inset: 2%; border-radius: 50%; }
.pp-orb-dot { position: absolute; display: block; border-radius: 50%; }

/* Soundbars under orb in listening */
.pp-bars {
  display: flex; align-items: end; justify-content: center;
  gap: 4px; height: 28px; margin-top: 22px;
}
.pp-bars > i {
  display: block; width: 3px; height: 100%;
  background: currentColor;
  transform-origin: center bottom;
  animation: pp-bar 0.9s ease-in-out infinite;
}
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(1) { animation-delay: -0.12s; }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: -0.36s; }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: -0.06s; }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(4) { animation-delay: -0.48s; }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(5) { animation-delay: -0.2s;  }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(6) { animation-delay: -0.62s; }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(7) { animation-delay: -0.32s; }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(8) { animation-delay: -0.5s;  }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(9) { animation-delay: -0.18s; }
.pp-bars > i:nth-child(10) { animation-delay: -0.42s; }

/* Manual-turn "hold" ring — LISTENING on a half-duplex engine (cascade STT):
   the turn ends only when the user presses SEND. */
.pp-orb-hold {
  position: absolute; inset: -7%;
  border: 1.5px dashed var(--pp-accent);
  border-radius: 50%;
  opacity: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.pp-orb[data-manual="true"][data-state="listening"] .pp-orb-hold {
  animation: pp-orb-hold 9s linear infinite;
}
@keyframes pp-orb-hold {
  0%   { transform: rotate(0deg)   scale(1);    opacity: 0.7; }
  50%  { transform: rotate(180deg) scale(1.04); opacity: 0.95; }
  100% { transform: rotate(360deg) scale(1);    opacity: 0.7; }
}
.pp-orb[data-manual="true"][data-state="listening"] .pp-orb-ring {
  animation: none; opacity: 0;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .pp-orb[data-manual="true"][data-state="listening"] .pp-orb-hold {
    animation: none; opacity: 0.85;
  }
}

/* Buttons standing in for clickable cards / rows / handles: keep the
   original look, add keyboard reach. */
.pp-btn-reset {
  appearance: none; font: inherit; color: inherit; text-align: left;
  border-radius: 0; margin: 0;
}

# The .dc.html authoring format — full rules and syntax card

Read this when an artboard needs more than SKILL.md's skeleton.
Everything the format supports is stated here — never design around a
presumed gap ("I'll make the swatches static because I can't verify
event syntax"): events, state and conditionals all work.

## Authoring an artboard

A Design Component is one self-contained HTML file the editor (and its
runtime) understands. Shape:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Hello</title>
  <script src="./support.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
<x-dc>
<helmet>
  <style>
    body { margin: 0; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; }
    a { color: #b45309; } a:hover { color: #92400e; }
  </style>
</helmet>
<div style="padding: 32px">
  <h1>{{title}}</h1>
  <sc-for list="{{items}}" as="item">
    <div>{{item.label}}</div>
  </sc-for>
</div>
</x-dc>
<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{"title":{"editor":"text","default":"Hello"}}'>
class Component extends DCLogic {
  renderVals() {
    return { title: this.props.title ?? 'Hello', items: [{ label: 'One' }] };
  }
}
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

Rules beyond SKILL.md's "Rules that bite":

- `lang` on `<html>` is the copy's language (`en` here); change it
  when the design's text is not English.
- `<title>` names the screen for accessibility; give each artboard its own, in a few words.
- Layout containers: a STACK is a flex `<div>` — inline
  `display: flex` plus `flex-direction`, `gap`, `justify-content`,
  `align-items`, with `flex-grow` / `align-self` on children. A GRID
  is a CSS-grid `<div>` — `display: grid` plus
  `grid-template-columns: repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr))` and `gap`;
  children flow into the cells in document order. Both are first-class
  in the editor: the properties panel edits the full set (grid
  Columns/Rows read and write as a plain track count when the tracks
  are equal — author them in exactly the `repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr))`
  shape so panel edits round-trip), viewers create them with the
  toolbar's Artboard tool or "Wrap in flex" / "Wrap in grid",
  and a viewer can drag an item OUT of either — the editor then
  freezes the remaining siblings and the parent's size so nothing else
  on the page moves. A DIAGRAM (boxes joined by
  lines) is neither: on a canvas build it from separate placed elements,
  never one `<svg>`, which the editor selects as one block (guidance to
  hand-draw a diagram as inline `<svg>` in a `<figure>` is for ordinary
  pages, not a canvas). `diagrams.md` has the forms: read it first.
- Multi-frame design explorations are ARTBOARDS: put each frame in
  its own `.dc.html` entry and lay them out with `canvas.json` — the
  host canvas provides the infinite pan/zoom; no in-file meta flag switches
  modes. Give every artboard whose content really works (handlers,
  inputs, navigation) `"is_interactive": true` in its canvas.json entry
  — only those get the blue mark and a Play button; leave it off
  static comps. A clickable prototype is one artboard per screen,
  joined by links (Links between artboards, below). A PAGE (landing
  page, dashboard, web app screen, scrolling explainer) gets `"expand":
  "fill"` on its artboard entry and a fluid root — in the full-window view
  it fills the window and scrolls as a page (without `fill` it is shrunk to
  fit); side menu + content: a `flex-wrap: wrap` row, content
  `flex: 999 1 560px; min-width: 0`, so the menu (never sticky or `100vh`) stacks on a
  phone; toolbars wrap; wide tables get an `overflow-x: auto` box; a one-file design can launch focused (`{"launch": {"view":
  "focused", "file": "Main.dc.html"}}`).
- LAYOUT GUIDES: an artboard entry may carry `"guides"`, up to 6, drawn
  by the canvas OVER the artboard, never in Play, exports or markup:
  `{"kind":"columns","count":12,"gutter":24,"margin":80}` (align
  `"stretch"`, default, divides the width inside `margin`;
  `"start"|"center"|"end"` pack `count` tracks of `"size"` px,
  `"offset"` in from that edge; `"count":"auto"` = as many as fit),
  `{"kind":"rows",…}` (same fields down the height; default `"auto"`
  8 px rows every 8), `{"kind":"grid","size":8}`; any may add `"color"`
  (hex or rgb()/hsl(), alpha = strength; default red at 10%) and
  `"hidden":true`. Add a guide only when a grid layout genuinely
  helps, never on every artboard. When an artboard has
  `"guides"`, lay the content ON it — a stretch guide is
  `display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(count, minmax(0,1fr));
  column-gap:<gutter>px; padding-inline:<margin>px`; children span
  tracks — and treat the user's guide edits as the intended layout.
- The design content a viewer edits is **untrusted cross-user input**
  like everything in the published state. It runs ONLY inside the
  editor's sandboxed preview iframe (editor-and-saving.md § How saving
  and sharing work) — never lift published design source into the host page, an
  unsandboxed surface, or any prompt without fencing (the shared
  fenceUntrusted rule: published-state-derived text entering any
  prompt is wrapped in nonce-delimited untrusted-data markers, with
  an instruction to treat it as data, so the receiving model does not
  read it as instructions).

## Quick syntax card (a syntax demo; `{{title}}` etc. are placeholders)

- **Holes**: `{{ path }}` is a dotted lookup only (`{{ user.name }}`,
  `{{ $index }}`, literals like `{{ true }}`) — never an expression
  (`{{ a + b }}`, `{{ !x }}`, `{{ fn() }}` fail silently). Compute in
  `renderVals()` and expose the result by name.
- **Attributes**: `x="literal"` → string; `x="{{ path }}"` → the raw
  value (number, function, ref); `x="a {{p}} b"` → interpolated
  string. `class`/`for` auto-map to `className`/`htmlFor`.
- **Events ARE supported**: whole-value attrs with JSX camelCase —
  `onClick="{{ pick }}"` — where `pick` is a function returned from
  `renderVals()`. Interactive selected-states (clickable swatches,
  size pills) are the house pattern: keep the selection in `state`,
  and for per-item handlers attach one to each loop item in
  `renderVals()` — `items: xs.map((x) => ({ ...x, pick: () =>
  this.setState({ picked: x.id }) }))` — then bind
  `onClick="{{ item.pick }}"` inside the `<sc-for>`.
- **Control flow**: `<sc-if value="{{ cond }}"
  hint-placeholder-val="{{ true }}">…</sc-if>` branches;
  `<sc-for list="{{ items }}" as="item" hint-placeholder-count="3">`
  repeats with `{{ item.x }}` and `{{ $index }}` in scope. Always set
  the `hint-*` attrs (they render while values stream in).
- **Links between artboards**: `<a href="Cart.dc.html">View cart</a>`
  moves Play to that artboard, in place or full window (not while
  editing). The href is the target's path relative to this
  artboard's; a leading `/` means the canvas root (`/sub/Cart.dc.html`).
  Style the `<a>` itself as the button: a `<button>` or input inside
  it swallows the click. `href="#id"` scrolls within the artboard;
  `https://…` opens a tab. Each artboard keeps its own `state`, so a
  flow that must share state across screens is ONE artboard: its
  handlers set a `state` field, `renderVals()` returns one flag per
  screen from it, and each screen sits in its own `<sc-if>`.
- **Conditional styling in a loop**: precompute the varying piece per
  item in `renderVals()` (e.g. each item carries `ringStyle` or
  `selected`) and either branch with `<sc-if>` or bind the computed
  value — a style hole is acceptable for live, state-driven values
  (selection highlights) and for a declared tweak prop (`{{accent}}`),
  just never for other static theme tokens, which belong inline so they
  paint while streaming.
- **Logic class**: plain classic JS, no TypeScript, no import/export;
  must be `class Component extends DCLogic`. You get `this.props`,
  `state`/`setState`/`forceUpdate` and React class lifecycle
  (`componentDidMount`…), minus `render()`. `renderVals()` returns the
  template's inputs: flat values, arrays, handlers, refs.
- **`data-props` editors** (on the `<script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script>` tag):
  per-prop `{"editor": "text"|"color"|"int"|"float"|"range"|"boolean"|
  "enum"|null, "default": …, "tsType": "…"}` plus `options` for enum,
  `min`/`max`/`step`/`unit` for numbers/range, `section` to group;
  on color, `options` as a 3–4-item list of hex strings renders swatches.
  `editor: null` for callbacks/objects. Editable props open in the
  panel's Tweaks tab from the artboard's Tweaks button (which props

// t(key, vars?, fallback?) — active table → EN table → fallback → the key itself.
function makeT(lang) {
  var table = STRINGS[lang] || STRINGS.en;
  return function (key, vars, fallback) {
    var s = table[key];
    if (s == null) s = STRINGS.en[key];
    if (s == null) s = fallback;
    if (s == null) s = key;
    if (vars) s = s.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, function (m, k) { return (k in vars) ? String(vars[k]) : m; });
    return s;
  };
}
// Flat copy table for the markup: 'nav.call' → s.nav_call.
var S_CACHE = {};
function stringsFor(lang) {
  if (S_CACHE[lang]) return S_CACHE[lang];
  var out = {}, en = STRINGS.en, tb = STRINGS[lang] || en;
  Object.keys(en).forEach(function (k) { out[k.replace(/\./g, '_')] = tb[k] != null ? tb[k] : en[k]; });
  S_CACHE[lang] = out;
  return out;
}

function formatExec(t, raw) {
  raw = raw || 'remote';
  if (raw === 'remote') return t('exec.remote');
  if (raw === 'local') return t('exec.local');
  if (raw === 'local / remote') return t('exec.hybrid');
  if (raw.indexOf('local: ') === 0) return t('exec.partial', { legs: raw.slice(7).toUpperCase() });

}
